questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That there was relevant courses I could attend.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find information, besides that starting date of our studies which was very vague. It seemed like the date changed all the time, and there was a lot of confusion about which week was "buddy week" and when courses started.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive assistance, besides information on studies and buddy programme.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I moved in with my partner, who lived there already. Therefore, housing was not an issue for me, but for future students I can recommend
finn.no
for finding housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You might pay a bit more, but it is definitely nice living more central, as it is a lot better connected than the usual student villages for Erasmus students like Sogn and Kringsjå.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy, you receive several informative emails, which has links to follow. You first have to be accepted by sending institution to a spot, and when this is done, you have to apply directly to UiO. When this is accepted, you receive emails with information on making a account in student web, where you can also apply for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their study guidance was very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the courses I registered for in the first place. Although it should be said that they made us believe that we probably weren't going to get a spot because other students were prioritised. This was stressing and confusing, and made many of us register for too many courses than we needed, just to be sure. 
The process of registering is challenging though, as you have to get the course accepted to your programme, which requires a few phone calls and emails. This is because you are not accepted for the courses as a default.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Register for a couple too many courses as a backup. You can also "drop" courses as you go, if you find it uninteresting or irrelevant. There is a couple of weeks from course start to deadline for registration, so you can change courses even if you started them. 
Also, be prepared to make som calls to get the courses in you programme at Studentweb.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Similar levels as at UCPH. 
However, in all courses the exam form was a closed book, which requires a lot of cramming. This was unusual for me, as I have not had these for a couple of years, and they are not necessarily the best exam forms for my kind of study. 
The one BA course I had required a lot more than MA, which I found unusual.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had lectures (ca. 3-4 hours per week/per course) and in two of the courses there was 2-3 hours of colloquia, where we could work with assignments and group work. I found that these were very beneficial.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOS5710 Advanced Cancer Biology
BIOS5610 Eukaryotic genes and genomes
BIOS3920 Forskningslitteratur i kreftbiologi

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOS5710. 
This was a really interesting course, with lots of variation in the lectures, and an amazing teacher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I dont thing there was something unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol was expensive, even with the NOK being weak. Concerts and clothes were surprisingly cheap, maybe because of the currency.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was an organisation called SiO, who arranged all sort of activities, both running club and flea markets for everyone, not only international students.
ESN was an organisation for Erasmus students and international students, that also arranges cultural trips and events. 
SiO (studerende i Oslo) also has gyms around the city, where you could get a membership for around 250 NOK/month.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Being a part of a sportsteam is an easy way to get to know Norwegians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes, and enjoy the nature. Notice when there is flea markets (e.g. Sundays at Grünerløkka). If you can, travel away from Oslo to see some other parts of Norway.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports team or club. Or during classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Norwegians can be very introvert and not very interested in talking to strangers and make new friends. This is challenging when you dont know anyone.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their national holiday 17th of may. And their joy of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to ask for student discount (clothes, beer, food, tickets)
Remember that all shops close on Sundays, and the few that are open are very very expensive, and very small. 
Know your own limits, and put value in close friends instead of many. You will need it. Exchange is hard, so know when enough is enough, because you will always miss out on something, and that is okay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that alcohol is only sold in limited time slots. Only beer is sold in regular stores, and if you want wine etc. you should go to vinmonopolet.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a small family of friends from across the world. When you are there for a limited amount of time, and dont know other people, close friends are the most comfortable and important thing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping calm in having fomo, and being comfortable about it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
